problem: Methods that combine 3D scene perception with VLM reasoning pass 3D information as text (coordinates, scene-graph strings), and the information lost in this conversion had never been measured. Prior 3D-encoder policies such as MTU3D avoid text but give up VLM reasoning.
motivation: Goal-directed navigation needs 3D scene understanding and reasoning to work together. Text serialization may discard the continuous geometric and semantic content in 3D encoder features. A controlled ablation that holds the encoder and VLM fixed and changes only the interface shows a representation gap.
key_idea: Project PQ3D's entity-level object and frontier query embeddings into a frozen VLM's hidden space as soft tokens with a lightweight MLP, and have the VLM output a frontier coordinate.
insight: With encoder and VLM fixed, soft tokens beat Text-Hint on val_seen (SPL +9.2 pp, p<0.0001; SR +7.5 pp, p=0.028). Adding LoRA to the text baseline (+1.6 SR, +2.2 SPL) or enriching the text with distance, direction and confidence (Rich-Text) does not close the gap, so the modality matters more than capacity or information content. On val_unseen the gain is mainly SR, and SPL falls 2.6 pp below Text-Hint because of longer paths.
method: Visual stream: frozen DINOv3 with a CompressionHead and PatchMerger (following AstraNav) gives 15 tokens per frame; a rolling buffer of 16 frames forms a 240x2048 visual memory.

3D stream: frozen PQ3D (MTU3D-adapted) does incremental instance segmentation, keeps an object bank and detects frontiers, and outputs a 768-d query embedding per object and per frontier (N about 128).
MLP projector: a 2-layer MLP (768→1408→2048) with GELU and LayerNorm maps each query to a soft token; about 4M parameters.
Scatter injection: placeholder tokens in the prompt are replaced at the embedding level by soft tokens. The input is [visual memory; frontier tokens then object tokens; text] into Qwen2.5-VL-3B.

Frontier decision: the VLM autoregressively generates a coordinate, which is snapped to the nearest frontier under a distance-ratio guardrail r=2. A rescue fallback handles an empty frontier set, and a GreedyGeodesicFollower executes the move.

Training: only the projector and LoRA (r=8, about 13M) are trained, with an SFT loss on 1,187 samples of frontier selections distilled from successful MTU3D episodes on OVON training scenes. Training uses 6 epochs on one RTX 4090.
Zero-shot transfer: one policy trained on OVON is reused on GOAT-Bench and SG3D, with benchmark-specific PQ3D stage-2 weights.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B (frozen, LoRA-adapted) + frozen PQ3D 3D encoder + frozen DINOv3 visual encoder + trainable MLP projector
setting.model_size: 3B VLM; about 17M trainable parameters (4M projector + 13M LoRA)
setting.training_data: 1,187 SFT samples (frontier-coordinate labels) from successful MTU3D episodes on OVON training scenes; PQ3D uses MTU3D pretrained weights
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 360x640 with pose, accumulated into 3D object and frontier queries plus 16-frame visual memory
setting.action_space: discrete (forward 0.25 m, turn left/right, look up/down) with high-level frontier waypoint selection executed by a GreedyGeodesicFollower
setting.privileged: none stated (uses PQ3D perception from RGB-D)

results: SoftNav reaches 74.2/68.3/66.7 SR on HM3D-OVON val_seen/synonyms/unseen, against 55.0/45.0/40.8 for the strongest prior method, MTU3D, and it has the highest SPL on all three splits. Zero-shot it gets 67.2/64.2 SR on GOAT-Bench val_seen/val_unseen and 47.2 s-SR on SG3D, but SPL is slightly below MTU3D on both. In the real world it succeeds in 19 of 30 trials on a Go2.
limitations: Only PQ3D and Qwen2.5-VL-3B were tested, so generality to other encoders and VLMs is unvalidated. Training uses only about 1.2k distilled samples, and SPL on val_unseen falls 2.6 pp below the Text-Hint baseline because paths are longer.

Evaluation sets are small (120 OVON episodes and 30 GOAT episodes per split, 30 real-world trials). Latency is about 1 s per step, and the policy is bounded by the teacher (MTU3D) and by PQ3D detection quality.
Cross-paradigm comparison involves different training regimes, and some baselines (AstraNav, text-interface methods) are excluded.
